title: Probe Calibration Under Adaptive Pressure: Can Attackers Fool the Free Detector?

original_idea.body: Probe Calibration Under Adaptive Pressure. Problem: cheap-probe results assumed non-adaptive attackers. Direction: train a linear jailbreak probe on an open model, craft simple adaptive prompts to minimize the probe's score while preserving the harmful payload, measure evasion rate; prompt-level search, no gradient access.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: adaptive-attack stress test of cheap probes informs whether to trust a proposed safety monitor.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Linear probe + prompt-level adaptive search; activation extraction + sklearn.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused evasion-rate measurement; a few coupled steps.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Neglected adaptive-robustness audit of a published monitor; external red-teaming.

low_compute.reasoning: Open-model activations + linear probe, single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Cheap-probe result published; adaptive stress test is the standard next question, plausibly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Cheap probes established on non-adaptive attacks; adaptive-evasion stress test is plausibly open.
